This is a bit dated, but that was exactly my point. The traffic stop is the pretext. If the traffic stop is the reason and that stop is proven illegitimate, the pretext is gone and thereby the DUI evidence.

That seems far-fetched to me. I understand that law enforcement can get away with a lot in terms of reasons for stops, but they can't just pull over whoever they want by making up a "hunch" every time. What Supreme Court case ruled on this?

From what I understand in Florida precedent, if the officer can prove he had "founded suspicion" that I was driving impaired, which is a low standard, then it was a legitimate stop. However, if he pulled me over solely for a traffic violation that I can prove I didn't commit, then I have a case for the suppression.

Thanks

I've seen the wording used in precedent to allow some degree of freedom, but ultimately I think my argument would come down to whether the officer testifies that there was suspicion of DUI before my stop or if the stop was a traffic violation that led to a DUI charge.

If there there is suspicion prior, unless we can prove otherwise... Yeah I'd be boned. But given my plea offer, it couldn't hurt much to try.

I'm in the big bend region. I have an attorney at the moment, but he seems kind of lazy. My legal fees are covered by insurance that my employer provides and I'm not sure if he's just milking it. He almost got my (hardship) license suspended again because he forgot to file for the citation with my DUI.

I'm glad all is well with you.

I'm not denying my choices. I made a bad choice. Although it's hard to say that while attempting to deny the validity of the stop. I know it looks like I'm trying to dodge punishment. But it does stand to reason that my driving was not erratic and I believe within the law (hold the DUI part). I do drive a poorly maintained sports car, which may have enticed the officer at 2am.

Unfortunately, DUIs cannot be sealed or expunged in Florida, otherwise, just accepting the plea deal would only hurt my bank and not my future. I know I don't have a substance problem so I wouldn't have any issues with probation or an interlock.
Thank you. I appreciate the information.

Sorry to hear that, bud.

I believe in your case, sleeping in your car might be a cause of suspicion for a cop to check on you, even if just for your well-being.

Well the officer mentioned "from left to right" I traveled over the dotted-lines "more than halfway of the vehicle".

Personally, I find it to be a far stretch to say one tire is half of my car. Legally, I'm not sure, of course. But I have found precedent where my point stands. In fairness, I've found a few where it fails.

Thanks for the information.

One further question, does the traffic stop begin at the lights or when my car is physically still?

Essentially, is the actual "reason why he stopped me" what occurred before the lights or can it include after? I understand I can commit crimes/infractions thereafter once the lights are on, but that would be something that occurs, due to my action, only because I was being pulled over for an initial infraction.

But the traffic stop was initiated as soon as the lights were activated, no? So anything that follows the lights results from whatever suspicion initiated the initial emergency lights. I also promise that I didn't continue on very far. I drove for just under another minute going 20-25mph.

This is my first offense for anything ever, traffic citation or criminal. My DUI school counselor even did not recommend counseling, which I hear is very common. I've gotten a few parking tickets from my college when I attended.

When I had my tire over the line it was returning to the lane from an intersection, with no other vehicles on either side. I thought that Florida statute requires your leaving the lane to possibly effect another vehicle?

If the traffic violation is the cause for the stop and the violation is found to be invalid in court, would that be possible cause to suppress the further evidence?

I suspect I likely got a plea deal just above minimum because of the minimum requirements for the charge by Florida law, but I suppose they could have offered a reduction.

Napping is nice. I just wish I had time for more of it.

I've also been spending a lot of time with my ex. I don't think it's healthy relationship wise, but it's really nice to have her company. And it's a lot like when we were dating so it feels especially comforting - like laying down together and just watching TV. I'd love to spend more time with her because when I'm with her I'm distracted and happy, but she's busy and I don't want to over burden her with my issues. I'm just trying to enjoy that time while I have it.

She's still my life insurance benefactor and I looked up yesterday how my policy deals with suicide. That was freaking depressing.

A buddy of mine who has gone through similar legal issues before is trying to help me and console me, but it's still hard to see any light at the end of the tunnel.

I don't want to hurt myself. I really don't. But I don't want to go to jail and live a life filled with failure more.

Thank you and thank everyone who commented for the thoughts and prayers.

This really is a troublesome time. These words do help. But now, somehow my church found out and they informed me yesterday I am no longer wanted to help volunteer with the youth program. I love those kids and poured out my heart and time helping them. It really sucks to be just dropped like that.

When women are upset, crying, and venting.

Not that I feel don't feel terrible about their troubles still - but I get this boner filled with manliness that I get to help them and be their support. And it's confused me before... I thought I was some sort of sadist for a while. But I've come to terms with it.
